title: Journey teardown on a canvas
promise: Compare how several products handle the same journey, laid out stage by stage on a board, ending in the gaps worth fixing first.
gives: A board with one lane per app per stage, scored and annotated, and a synthesis for each stage.
needs: Screens to compare. Miro is optional.
ask: Tear down how these four apps handle the weekly shop.
demoNote: The agent lays out four apps across three stages, annotates every screen and scores each lane. When it ends, drag the board, zoom it and filter the notes.
clipTitle: A competitor teardown *laid out by journey*
clipLine: One lane per app, per stage. Your product last, under the best example.

example.label: Four grocery apps, three stages
example.note: Twelve lanes, twenty-four screens and sixty notes. Tangelo is the last lane in every stage.

when: You are about to propose changes to a journey and need to know what good looks like.
You can get screens for at least three products, your own included.
A team keeps arguing from memory about what competitors do.
skip: You need market share, pricing or strategy. This compares screens, not businesses.
You have fewer than three products, or cannot get screens for the journey.
The journey happens mostly outside the product, such as in sales calls.

inputs.name: The journey and its stages
inputs.note: For example: open the app, build the basket, pay.

inputs.name: Screens for each app at each stage
inputs.note: Image files or links, each with a capture date. Your own product included.

inputs.name: What you want to learn
inputs.note: One question keeps the board from turning into a gallery.

outputs.name: board.html
outputs.note: The whole teardown as one file you can pan, zoom and filter.

outputs.name: A Miro board
outputs.note: The same layout, built through the Miro connector when it is connected.

outputs.name: teardown.json
outputs.note: Scores, notes, patterns and gaps as data, ready for the PRD skill.

steps.title: Fix the vocabulary first
steps.body: The legend and the scoring rubric go onto the board before a single screen is read, so every later note uses the same four labels and five dimensions.

steps.title: Lay out one lane per app per stage
steps.body: Stages run down the board and apps stack inside each. Your own product is always the last lane in a stage, directly under the best examples.

steps.title: Annotate each screen, three notes at most
steps.body: Each note is Good, Friction, Note or Idea. It names what is on the screen and says why that matters.

steps.title: Score with a reason
steps.body: Five dimensions, whole numbers from 1 to 5, each with a one-line reason. No reason, no score.

steps.title: Synthesise each stage
steps.body: Best in class, patterns with the apps they were seen in, the ideal flow, and your gaps with a priority and a benchmark.

steps.title: Say what is missing
steps.body: Screens are counted per lane, thin lanes are flagged, and anything taken from a help page rather than a real screen is marked.

checks.name: Every score has a reason
checks.note: The checker rejects a score with no written reason, and any score that is not a whole number from 1 to 5.

checks.name: Every pattern lists where it was seen
checks.note: A pattern has to name at least two apps, and each must exist on the board.

checks.name: Every gap names a benchmark
checks.note: A gap must say what you do today, the fix, and which app shows the fix working.

checks.name: No screen has more than three notes
checks.note: More than three and nobody reads any of them.

checks.name: Your product is the last lane in every stage
checks.note: So the contrast with the best example is always in the same place.

checks.name: Coverage is stated
checks.note: Lanes with fewer than two screens are flagged on the board, not hidden.

checks.name: Your product was scored by the same rubric
checks.note: Read your own lanes last and check you were not kinder to them.

failures.title: Scores look more exact than they are
failures.body: One reader scored every lane. The numbers rank screens against each other. They are not measurements.
failures.catch: Use the scores to choose what to look at, then read the notes. Never quote a score without its reason.

failures.title: Screens go stale
failures.body: Apps change every week. A teardown is a photograph with a date on it.
failures.catch: Every lane carries its capture date. Capture again anything older than a quarter before you rely on it.

failures.title: It describes screens, not outcomes
failures.body: A screen can look clear and still convert badly. The board cannot see that.
failures.catch: Treat patterns as hypotheses. The experiment readout is where they get tested.

run.by: A fresh agent session, given only the skill folder and the 24 input screens. Nobody answered its questions.
run.note: Run twice. The first run passed and listed 15 gaps in the instructions. They were fixed, the checker was made stricter, and the second run produced the board shown here.

carousel.title: One lane per app, *per stage*
carousel.body: Four apps across three stages of the same journey. Here is the first stage: four lanes, read left to right.

carousel.title: Up to three notes *on every screen*
carousel.body: Good, friction, note or idea. Each note names what is on the screen and why it matters.

carousel.title: Your product is *always last*
carousel.body: It sits under the best examples in every stage, so the contrast is in the same place every time.

carousel.title: Five scores, *each with a reason*
carousel.body: No reason, no score. The scores rank the lanes. They do not pretend to measure them.

carousel.title: Every stage ends in *gaps to fix*
carousel.body: Patterns to adopt, patterns to avoid, the ideal flow, and your gaps by priority.

carousel.title: The whole board, *yours to open*
carousel.body: Drag it, zoom it, filter the notes. It is one HTML file you can send to anyone.
